entries.name: delay
entries.description: an empty span that consumes time

params.description: Composition: an empty span that consumes time.
params.title: DelayAction

entries.name: grasp
entries.description: reach an item with a body's point (a hand) and take it, keeping its pose

params.description:
``by`` (a body's point: a hand) reaches ``item``'s grip and takes it.

``item`` is an entity id, with ``@<point>`` the grip (a bone of its rig,
or ``u,v`` a fraction of its drawing); unset: its ``grip`` bone, else its
stage point. ``by`` with no ``@`` is the far end of the body (an arm's
hand). The item is held from ``start + reach`` on, and over the retract it
turns to how the hand holds things (``align``): drawn as it is, upright
along the hand's part, the way a socket holds it; ``align: false`` keeps
the angle it was taken at.

>>> GraspAction(by="stu@hand_r", item="musket").reach == DFLT_REACH
True
params.title: GraspAction

entries.name: handover
entries.description: give a held item to another holder (a hand, a socket)

params.description:
The hand holding ``item`` gives it to ``to`` (a hand, or a socket).

``meet`` is where the two meet, as a fraction of the way from the giver's
hand to the receiver's: ``1`` (the default) puts it into the receiver's
point, which does not move (a figurine's hand, a waiting hand); below 1
both hands reach and the receiver takes it where they meet (and turns it
as a ``grasp`` does, ``align``).

>>> HandoverAction(item="sword", to="nap/arm_r/weapon").meet
1.0
params.title: HandoverAction

entries.name: join
entries.description: enforce a declared joint from an instant on

params.description:
The declared joint named ``joint`` is enforced from ``at`` on.

>>> JoinAction(joint="grip", at=1.0).at
1.0
params.title: JoinAction

ExtensionAction.description:
An action of a kind the core does not define: the IR's one open member.

The schema's ``Action`` union selects this for any ``kind`` other than the
core's (ADR 0001 decision 2). When a genre has REGISTERED that kind
(:func:`an.genres.registry.register_action_kind`), validating a document
yields the registered model instead — a ``PlayAction`` for ``kind: play`` —
so code downstream sees typed actions. Before registration the action
stays an ``ExtensionAction``: its fields are kept as extras and round-trip
byte for byte, and :meth:`resolved` (called by ``flatten``, ``an validate``
and the compiler) refuses it naming the genre that provides it.

Every genre's action model subclasses this, which is what lets a typed
instance sit in the union and serialize with its own fields.

>>> ExtensionAction(kind="wave", target="flag").model_dump()
{'name': None, 'kind': 'wave', 'target': 'flag'}
ExtensionAction.title: ExtensionAction

entries.name: pin
entries.description: hold a body's point exactly at a point for a span (a rod, a nail)

params.description:
``point`` (``body[@point]``) held exactly at ``to`` for ``duration``
seconds (``None``: to the shot's end). It frees the body ``point`` is on
for the span: a pinned cup goes to the hand, wherever it was staged.

>>> PinAction(point="cup", to="paul/fore_r@hand").to
'paul/fore_r@hand'
params.title: PinAction

entries.name: place
entries.description: bring a held item onto the ground, a socket or a point, and let it go there

params.description:
The hand holding ``item`` puts it ``onto`` a target and lets it go.

``onto`` is ``ground`` (straight down, at floor height), ``ground@x`` (at
stage ``x``), a body's point (a socket: the item's grip goes there, its
frame aligned with the socket's), a body's surface (``crate@surface``, or
``crate@surface@f`` at that fraction along it: lying on its top as on the
ground, held by that body from then on, an#536) or ``world@x,y`` (hung on
a point).
``item@<point>`` names the item's point that touches the target (default:
its grip on a socket, its lowest point on the ground). ``rotation``: the
item's rotation where it rests (radians, the stage's; default: the angle it
last rested at on the ground, else the nearest quarter turn; in a socket,
the socket's own). In a socket it is the angle the item comes to rest at
(a musket aimed at someone, a sabre raised), held relative to the socket
from then on, so it turns with it.

>>> PlaceAction(item="musket", onto="nap/arm_r/weapon").by is None
True
params.title: PlaceAction

entries.name: pull
entries.description: draw a body's point toward a point or along a path (a string)

params.description:
``point`` drawn toward ``to`` (a point, or a path of stage points walked
at an even speed over the span) for ``over`` seconds (``None``: to the
shot's end), as close as the joints allow; ``give`` is the string's
softness (compliance, px per unit of pull).

>>> PullAction(point="puppet/hand_l", to=[[0, -200], [100, -200]], over=2.0).over
2.0
params.title: PullAction

entries.name: reframe
entries.description: move a world member to another frame of reference at an instant, keeping its place in the world; optionally flying free under gravity

params.description:
Member ``target`` leaves its frame for ``to`` at ``at`` (shot seconds).

>>> ReframeAction(target="bottle", to="world").keep
'world'
params.title: ReframeAction

entries.name: release
entries.description: let a held item go: it falls, or is tossed, onto the ground

params.description:
The hand holding ``item`` lets it go at ``at``: it falls with the
velocity it had onto the ground, or is tossed ``onto: ground@x`` on an
arc ``arc`` px high, and lands at ``rotation`` (default: as in ``place``).

>>> ReleaseAction(item="cup", at=1.0).onto is None
True
params.title: ReleaseAction

entries.name: swap
entries.description: take the item a holder has and give it another in its place

params.description:
``by`` takes ``take`` from ``holder`` and the hand holding ``give``

entries.name: environment
entries.description: the set / background: planes, with parallax, drawn behind
entries.usage: its nodes are stage.node nodes; ref keys into the 'environments' store

entries.name: prop
entries.description: a prop or piece of set dressing; also stroked paths and text blocks
entries.usage: its nodes are stage.node nodes; ref keys into the 'props' store

entries.name: voice
entries.description: a voice the audio pipeline speaks with; draws nothing
entries.usage: ; ref keys into the 'voices' store

entries.name: meta
entries.description: the film's header
entries.usage: meta: {title, author, duration, fps, resolution, default_renderer, notes, default_easing, step_hz, style_pack, sounds, captions, closing_transition}

entries.name: meta.captions
entries.description: captions derived from the dialogue
entries.usage: meta.captions (optional): captions built at render time from the dialogue's word timings — {} for the defaults, or {highlight: '#rrggbb', color, size, anchor, max_chars, max_lines, burn, sidecar, strict}. Never add caption text entities by hand: they are derived from the dialogue.

entries.name: meta.closing_transition
entries.description: how the film ends
entries.usage: meta.closing_transition (optional): how the film ENDS — {kind: 'fade', duration: seconds, color: '#rrggbb'}: the last shot's last duration fades to color (its final frame IS the color) and the sound fades with it; the film's length is unchanged. Omitted (or 'cut') = it ends on its last frame. A dissolve is refused.

entries.name: meta.sounds
entries.description: sounds on the film's clock (a music bed)
entries.usage: meta.sounds (optional): the same cue shape in FILM time — a music bed is {sound: <key>, loop: true, duck_db: -12, fade_in, fade_out}; duck_db ducks it under every dialogue line.

entries.name: shot
entries.description: one shot of the timeline
entries.usage: timeline: a list of shots, each with id (string, unique), renderer ("cutout" | "stage" | "manim" | "motion_graphics" | "whiteboard"), duration (seconds, float), camera, entities, actions, dialogue, narration, transition, sounds

entries.name: shot.actions
entries.description: the shot's animation
entries.usage: actions: list of action dicts whose kind is a registered action kind (the composites sequence, parallel, delay and loop hold children).

entries.name: shot.actions.easing
entries.description: how a tween moves through time
entries.usage: A tween's easing is a registered easing name, a cubic-Bézier 4-list [cx1, cy1, cx2, cy2], or a parametrised curve such as 'cubic-bezier(…)' or 'steps(n)'.

entries.name: shot.actions.property
entries.description: what a set or tween animates
entries.usage: A tween/set action's property is EITHER a transform: alpha, dash_offset, perspective, pivot_x, pivot_y, plane_fade_end, plane_fade_start, rotation, rotation_rad, rotation_x, scale_x, scale_y, skew_x, skew_y, trim_end, trim_start, x, y — OR 'tint', a per-node colour MULTIPLY whose value is a '#rrggbb' string (the compiler expands it into three numeric channels, so a tween between two colours interpolates per channel; like 'alpha' it cascades to the target's parts). 'alpha' is the fade primitive and cascades to a character's parts. On a text block, 'text' swaps a replacement set's string ('texts', unit 'block'; the value is a key) and 'value' is a counter block's number ('counter'; set or tween a number, lowered at compile to the strings the frames show). Any other property (opacity, visible, color, width, ...) is refused at compile. A tween with no 'from' starts at the property's rest value: 1.0 for scale_x / scale_y / alpha / trim_end / perspective, '#ffffff' for tint, 0.0 for the rest. rotation_x / perspective / plane_fade_start / plane_fade_end tilt the node's plane away from the camera (radians, frame heights, plane px), and then pivot_y slides its content along the plane. A tween with no 'easing' takes the scene's meta.default_easing when set.

entries.name: shot.camera
entries.description: the shot's camera
entries.usage: camera: {move: <a camera move>, ...} or explicit {keys: [...]}

entries.name: shot.camera.follow
entries.description: a camera that follows an entity
entries.usage: camera.follow (optional): {target: <entity id or node path>, axes: x|y|xy} — the camera tracks the target, keeping it where it stood at the shot's start (a walk across a long set); planes parallax with it. Instead of a move or keys (hold is fine); a shake layers on top.

entries.name: shot.camera.shake
entries.description: a jolt of the frame inside the shot
entries.usage: camera.shake (optional): jolts of the frame layered on the move or keys — [{at: s, duration: 0.4, amplitude: 0.015, frequency: 24, decay: true, seed: 0}], amplitude a fraction of the frame height; for an impact, a slam, an explosion. The frame is at rest before `at` and after the end; shakes may not overlap or run past the shot.

entries.name: shot.dialogue
entries.description: who says what, and when
entries.usage: dialogue: list of {speaker, text, emotion, voice_ref, pause, at, direction, ...}. Lines play back to back from the shot start. 'pause' (seconds) is silence before a line, after the previous one ends — a beat, a look, a hesitation belongs here, NOT in a new shot. 'at' (seconds) starts a line at that shot time instead; a line takes one or the other, never both (to switch, delete the one you are replacing in the same patch list). 'start' and 'duration' are stamped by the audio pipeline from these on every render — never patch them.

entries.name: shot.dialogue.direction
entries.description: how a line is delivered
entries.usage: direction (optional) is a list of delivery cues — ['excited'], ['sighs', 'annoyed'] — that an expressive TTS voice performs; it is never spoken as text and never shown in captions.

entries.name: shot.entities
entries.description: who and what is on stage
entries.usage: entities: list of {kind, id, store, ref, ...}; kind MUST be a registered entity kind. A prop needs a PropDescriptor in the props store; it has no placeholder rig, so an unknown ref raises rather than drawing a person.

entries.name: shot.narration
entries.description: a narrator's lines (not implemented)
entries.usage: narration: list (same shape as dialogue, no speaker pin). NOT IMPLEMENTED — the audio pipeline walks dialogue only, and a shot with narration RAISES. To add a narrator, emit a dialogue line whose speaker is not an entity in the shot; it gets audio and no lip-sync.

entries.name: shot.sounds
entries.description: sound effects on the shot's clock
entries.usage: sounds (optional): SFX cues in SHOT-local time — [{sound: <key in the sounds store>, at, [duration], [gain_db], [loop], [fade_in], [fade_out], [duck_db]}]. Never invent a sound key.

entries.name: shot.transition
entries.description: how a shot is entered
entries.usage: transition (optional): how the shot is ENTERED — {kind: "cut" | "fade" | "dissolve" | "wipe", duration: seconds, color: '#rrggbb'}. Omitted = a hard cut. 'fade' dips through color (half out of the previous shot, half into this one; on the first shot, a fade up). 'dissolve' overlaps the two shots by duration, so the film gets that much shorter; never on the first shot. 'wipe' overlaps the same way, but a hard edge sweeps across the frame in direction ('left', 'right', 'up' or 'down': the way the edge travels). A shot must be long enough to hold its own transition and the next shot's.

entries.name: noop
entries.title: no-op
entries.description: do nothing, and record it: the last link of a chain whose aspect does not apply to the asset

entries.name: framing2d
entries.description: a 2D framing of a flat picture: position, zoom (log), roll (angle)
entries.usage: axes: x (frame widths, linear), y (frame heights, linear), zoom (ratio, log), rotation (rad, angle)

entries.name: orbit3d
entries.description: an orbit camera around a 3D target: azimuth and elevation (angles), distance (log)
entries.usage: axes: azimuth (rad, angle), elevation (rad, angle), distance (scene units, log), target_x (scene units, linear), target_y (scene units, linear), target_z (scene units, linear)
